heading: The dispositions
text:
## The dispositions [LERR.1]

**One axis, ordered by how much execution is abandoned.** A feature picks
exactly one rung, and the rung says what the condition costs:

| | Disposition | Abandoned |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | **Compile error** ([LERR.1.1]) | nothing — the program never runs |
| 2 | **Bounds refusal** ([LERR.1.5]) | nothing — the operation does not happen |
| 3 | **Errors-as-values** ([LERR.1.2]) | nothing — the error is ordinary data |
| 4 | **Absence** ([LERR.1.3]) | the expression; the rule does not fire |
| 5 | **TypeError** ([LERR.1.4]) | the activation |
| 6 | **ComputationError** ([LERR.1.4]) | the activation |
| 7 | **EngineError** ([LERR.1.4]) | the tier |

**Every rung tells someone**, so that is not what varies. A compile error
reaches the author; a bounds refusal returns `DS_ERR_CONTRACT_BREACH` to the
caller ([RTCT.7.2]); an error-as-value is a fact rules match on; rungs 5 and 6 take
all three fault surfaces — *record the event, assert the fault fact, invoke the
integrator callback* ([RFCS.21.1], [LERR.9.1]) — and rung 7 takes the first and
the last, because the tier it halts has no working memory to assert into. What
varies is the cost.

**Rungs 5 and 6 tie on cost and differ in why**, which is the whole reason they
are separate kinds rather than one: a consumer needs to know whether the data
was wrong or the computation had no answer. Rungs 2 and 3 also tie at nothing,
and are ordered by whether the caller or the program is the one that learns.

**Rungs 4–7 are the five vocabularies** of the absent-value and fault model;
rungs 1–3 are the ones that model does not reach, because they are not faults.

alloy.name: lerr_1__before
alloy.note: Kind priority. EngineError first is [LERR.1]'s order; TypeError before trap is [LNUL.4.2]'s choice, since [LERR.1] ties the two on cost. V5 as stated by [LNUL.4.2] and [IRET.9.5]: a false decides wherever it stands; otherwise the faults resolve by kind, then by the fields of the record (T2I); the evaluation order is free.

alloy.name: lerr_1__faults
alloy.note: The three fault kinds a `where` can meet: [LERR.1]'s rungs 5, 6 and 7.

idris.note: The three fault kinds a `where` can meet: [LERR.1]'s rungs 5, 6 and 7.

idris.name: lerr_1__prio
idris.note: EngineError first is [LERR.1]'s own order: it abandons the tier, the other two the activation. TypeError before trap is [LNUL.4.2]'s choice, since [LERR.1] ties rungs 5 and 6 on cost; swapping the two leaves every theorem of the module standing (TEETH T4). V5 as stated by [LNUL.4.2] and [IRET.9.5]: a false decides wherever it stands; otherwise the faults resolve by kind, then by the fields of the record (T2I); the evaluation order is free.

idris.name: lerr_1__prio_inj
idris.note: Distinct kinds have distinct priorities: the order on kinds is total.
